submission, planning staff advised that an official plan amendment was no longer required
and recommended revising the design to comply with the new SGA 3 zoning regulations. After
further discussions with staff, it was determined that a zoning by-law amendment would still
be required to introduce site-specific zoning regulations to address the unique site constraints,
which are shown on this slide.
The site is in a regular L shape and has varying lot widths, which have presented unique design
challenges for the development.
The narrow middle section and angled front, rear and easterly lot lines complicate physical
separation and setback compliance.
These constraints have required adjustments in the building's design to ensure functional
use while adhering as closely as possible to the SGA 3 zoning regulations.
As part of the redesign of the proposal, we have made several key modifications to the
proposal to address staff comments and site constraints.
The ground floor has been increased from the ground floor setback has increased from 4.8
to 6 metres to enhance the pedestrian environment.
The building has shifted eastward, allowing for a larger westerly side yard.
Physical separation is now met for all floors on the west side, with the exception of stories
19 to 28, where a 2-metre reduction is requested to provide for adequate unit sizes.
Step backs and building length were modified to better align with the zoning categories
for stories 7 to 12, 13 to 18, and 19 to 28.
garage was redesigned to create a larger interior side yard setback on the west side adjacent
the parking garage, which was increased from what was originally one metre to three metres.
Portions of the rear and east side yard setbacks adjacent to the parking garage still require
reduced setbacks to allow for an efficient parking garage layout. Two one-way driveways
were introduced to maintain functionality, and the bicycle parking, the proposal now
fully meets the required bicycle parking. The number of requested variances has been
reduced from 16 to 9 and are mainly related to the easterly lot line pinch point and the
front yard setback on the upper floors to facilitate the cantilever design.
This slide shows the amenity spaces that are being proposed, which they offer a range of
indoor and outdoor amenity spaces.
Indoor space, over 500 square metres, including a gym, lounge and games room.
And outdoor spaces, an expansive rooftop terrace, shared terraces, private balconies and seating
areas offering over 1,500 square metres of combined outdoor space.
So some of the key design elements to the proposal is a recessed ground floor commercial
space that will create an inviting public area, the building's unique cantilevered and
angled design to enhance the appeal and streetscape, urban plazas and patios for commercial use,
And in conclusion, the proposed development aligns with the broader goals of growing together
land use framework despite the site's unique constraints.
We believe this project will enhance the Mill Street area by adding much needed housing
supply and improving the pedestrian environment, contributing positively to Kitchener's long-term
growth.
